channel.title: NMWWD — Insights
channel.description: Research, data, and prevention reporting on wrong-way driving — from a Phoenix-based road-safety nonprofit.

item.title: Red reflectors, WRONG WAY signs, and arrows: how the road tells you to stop
item.description: A plain guide to wrong-way signs, red reflectors, and pavement arrows on Arizona ramps, and what each one means for a driver who sees it.

item.title: Visitor season is here: sharing Phoenix freeways with drivers who don't know them
item.description: Fall and winter bring visitors and snowbirds to Phoenix freeways. Here's how locals and newcomers can lower wrong-way driver risk in Arizona this season.

item.title: How to support wrong-way prevention where you live
item.description: Most of this work happens at the state and municipal level, which means an individual can have more influence than you'd expect.

item.title: Talking with a parent about night driving
item.description: One of the hardest conversations families have. Here's an approach that tends to work better than the one most people try first.

item.title: What a wrong-way alert app can and can't do
item.description: In-vehicle warning fills a real gap in roadside infrastructure. It also has honest limits, and we'd rather state them than oversell.

item.title: Why unfamiliar roads raise wrong-way risk
item.description: Drivers far from home are overrepresented in these crashes. The implication is that interchanges have to be readable by people who have never seen them.

item.title: Night, dawn, and dusk: when wrong-way crashes happen
item.description: These crashes cluster hard in specific conditions. That clustering is the reason focused prevention works.

item.title: Older drivers and wrong-way risk
item.description: Older drivers are overrepresented in fatal wrong-way crashes. The reasons are specific and mostly addressable — and the conversation deserves more care than it usually gets.

item.title: The off-ramp problem: where wrong-way entries actually begin
item.description: Almost every wrong-way trip starts at one identifiable point. That's the strongest argument for engineering solutions over awareness alone.

item.title: What to do if you see a wrong-way driver
item.description: The right actions take seconds and are worth knowing before you need them. Read this once and it may be there when it counts.

item.title: Impairment and wrong-way driving
item.description: Alcohol-impaired drivers are consistently overrepresented in fatal wrong-way crashes. Understanding why points directly at what prevention has to accomplish.

item.title: How Arizona's wrong-way detection system actually works
item.description: ADOT built one of the country's first large thermal-camera wrong-way detection systems on I-17. Here's what it does and what it has found.

item.title: Why wrong-way crashes are so much deadlier than other crashes
item.description: It isn't bad luck. It's physics, geometry, and reaction time working together in the worst possible combination.

item.title: Wrong-way crashes are rising. Here's what the data shows.
item.description: Fatal wrong-way crashes on U.S. divided highways roughly doubled between 2014 and 2023. The numbers are small, the trend is not, and the pattern points at prevention.
